name: Dr. Abdullah Alshammari
title: Assistant Professor
bio:
Biography

Dr. Abdullah joined Dubai Medical College for Girls in 2023 as a full-time assistant professor in the nursing program. He earned his Bachelor of Nursing Science from Jordan University of Science and Technology, Jordan, a Master of Community Health Nursing from Jordan University of Science and Technology, Jordan, and a Ph.D. in Community Health Nursing at the University of Szeged, Hungary.

Dr. Abdullah worked in several hospital areas as a registered nurse, gaining clinical experience in emergency departments, intensive care, geriatric, psychology, home health, school health, and outpatient mental health. Dr. Abdullah’s teaching experience was commissioned at Jordan University of Science and Technology, Jordan, in 2012, where he taught Fundamentals of Nursing, Comprehensive Health Assessment, Adult Health Nursing I, Community Health Nursing, and Intensive Clinical Training. Dr. Abdullah’s research interests include Health Behaviours and Adolescents Mental Health. Dr. Abdullah was a research assistant in several projects, such as the Defence Threat Reduction Agency for Biological Threats Reduction Program, USAID, Eco Health Alliance, PREDICT Project, Jordan University of Science and Technology, World Health Organization, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, and John Hopkins University Bloomberg School of Public Health. Dr. Abdullah also worked as a risk manager and quality coordinator for hospitals.

bio:
Biography

Dr. Zahraa Khalifa is an Assistant Professor of Pharmaceutical Sciences at the College of Pharmacy, Dubai Medical University. She earned her PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences, with a focus on Drug Delivery, from the University of Strathclyde, UK, where her doctoral research focused on the development of multimodal vaccine delivery systems. With more than 15 years of academic experience, she is actively involved in teaching, student mentorship, and the development of innovative learning approaches. Dr. Zahraa is a Fellow of Advance HE, reflecting her commitment to excellence in higher education. name: Dr. Arina Ziganshina

bio:
Biography

Dr. Arina Ziganshina, MD, PhD, MHPE, SFHEA is an Assistant Professor, Head of the Examination and Assessment Unit at Dubai Medical University Chair of Assessment Committee at the College of Medicine. She earned her MD and PhD in Clinical Medicine from Kazan State Medical University (Russia), and an MHPE from Gulf Medical University.

Previously at Kazan State Medical University, she conducted clinical teaching and research spanning medical education and pediatric gastroenterology, while contributing to curriculum design, and building assessment systems. Dr. Ziganshina has presented internationally, including AMEE and the Canadian Conference on Medical Education (2021), and the Middle East & North America Higher Education Leadership Forum, International Educational Conference, Abu Dhabi (2024) and WFME World Conference (2025). Her scholarship focuses on assessment, internationalization, and educational technologies. She leads Journal Clubs and CPD events on assessment, ed-tech, and internationalization, and serves as a peer reviewer (e.g., BMC Medical Education). He has held prestigious academic positions worldwide, including roles at King Saud University, King Faisal University as one of the main founders of the College of Clinical Pharmacy, and most recently, Qatar University, where he served as Head of the Pharmaceutical Sciences Department. In addition, he worked as a Senior Scientist at Virginia State University and Polytechnic Institute (Blacksburg, VA) and Analytical Biochemistry Laboratories (Columbia, Missouri) in the USA. name: Ms. Aisha Abdullah
title: Student Affairs Assistant
bio:
Biography

With extensive experience in administrative roles within academic and medical institutions, I have been serving as an Administrative Officer at Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy since 2008. Over the years, I have developed strong expertise in student services, alumni affairs, faculty support, and academic operations.

In my role as Admission Officer for the College of Nursing, I guide newly admitted students through the onboarding process by addressing inquiries, ensuring timely submission of documents, and coordinating communication between students and the admissions team. I also provide essential information on college policies, timelines, and academic requirements while maintaining accurate records and documentation.

As part of Alumni Affairs for MPharm and BPharm programs, I manage certificate verifications, liaise with Data Flow Group, handle alumni document requests, and prepare graduation and clearance materials. I maintain updated alumni databases for educational and immigration needs, support golden residency procedures, and assist with annual surveys and ministry reports.

In addition, I handle Faculty Affairs, where I oversee the maintenance of faculty and staff files, process visa and health insurance documentation, and prepare official letters such as salary certificates and statements.

Prior to this, I worked as an Administrative Secretary at Dubai Specialized Medical Center & Medical Research Labs (2002–2006), where I managed correspondence, coordinated staff schedules and internal meetings, maintained attendance and inventory records, and supported various documentation tasks.

I hold a Higher Secondary School Certificate (2004) and have completed certifications in MS Office (2002) and ICDL, equipping me with strong digital and administrative skills to support operations effectively.

name: Dr. Bassam Atallah
title: Associate Professor, Associate Dean - Clinical Affairs
bio:
Biography

Dr Atallah is the Associate Dean for Clinical Affairs at Dubai Medical University. Prior to joining DMU he served as Cardiovascular Senior Pharmacotherapy Specialist at Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi and Clinical Associate Professor at Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine. Prior to joining Cleveland Clinic he was on faculty as Assistant Professor of Clinical Pharmacy at King Saud bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences (KSAU-HS) in Riyadh. Dr. Atallah received his PharmD from Bernard J. Dunn School of Pharmacy in Virginia and completed an ASHP accredited post graduate residency at Winchester Medical Center in Virginia. He was awarded the “Graduate of the Last Decade” award by his alma mater. Dr. Atallah is board certified in pharmacotherapy with added qualifications in Cardiology. He also holds an advanced antithrombotic management certificate from ASHP. Dr Atallah is a fellow of the Heart Failure Society of America (HFSA) and the American College of Clinical Pharmacy (ACCP). He has several publications and presentations at national and international conferences. He was awarded the 2021 ACCP Cardiology PRN international award. His research interests are in various aspects of cardiovascular pharmacotherapy with focus on antithrombotic therapy, heart failure and hyperlipidemia.

Education

  • Bachelor of Science in Biology, American University of Beirut, Lebanon (2003-2006)

name: Dr. Khaled Elmasry
title: Assistant Professor of Human Anatomy and Embryology
bio:
Biography

Dr. Khaled Elmasry, MD, MSc, PhD, is an Assistant Professor of Human Anatomy and Embryology in the Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine, Dubai Medical University, Dubai, UAE. He graduated with an MBBS (MD) with Honors from the Faculty of Medicine, Mansoura University, Egypt (2007) and completed an MSc in Basic Medical Sciences (Human Anatomy and Embryology) at the same university (2011). Dr. Elmasry earned his PhD in Biomedical Sciences (Cellular Biology and Anatomy) from the Medical College of Georgia at Augusta University, USA (2018). His postgraduate training includes postdoctoral fellowships at Schepens Eye Research Institute, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA (2018-2019) and at Oakland University’s Eye Research Institute, Rochester, MI, USA (2021–2022).

Dr. Elmasry previously served as an Assistant Professor of Human Anatomy and Embryology at Mansoura Faculty of Medicine, Mansoura University, Mansoura, Egypt (2019–2024) and later at the Dental College of Georgia, Augusta University (2022–2025), where he directed courses in craniofacial and gastrointestinal anatomy and led Bio clinical seminars. His research focuses on extracellular vesicle signaling, hypoxia and inflammation in diabetic retinopathy, bone morphogenetic proteins, retinal neurovascular physiology, and the therapeutic effects of natural compounds. He has authored numerous peer‑reviewed articles and received multiple awards, including the Vision Discovery Institute award of excellence in vision research and the 2018 People’s Choice Prize in the Three‑Minute Thesis competition. He was also awarded the New Faculty Teaching Excellence Award from the Dental College of Georgia (2024). Dr. Elmasry is an active member of professional societies, such as the Egyptian Medical Syndicate and the Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology.

Teaching & Service
  • Dubai Medical University (2025‑Present) – Assistant Professor of Human Anatomy & Embryology, Department of Biomedical Sciences, teaching Human Structure and Function 2 to Year 3 and Year 4 medical students (Batch 37 and Batch 36).
  • Augusta University, Dental College of Georgia (2022‑2025) – Course director for the Craniofacial Complex Anatomy course (BMCC 5201) and the Gastrointestinal Tract System Module (D2). Lead faculty for Bioclinical Seminar courses (BMBS 5201/5403). Participated in courses on cardiovascular, respiratory, and neuroscience systems.
  • Mansoura University, Egypt (2008‑2024) – Instructor and later assistant professor teaching Human Anatomy and Embryology, surgical anatomy and anatomy courses for dental and physical therapy students. Provided problem‑based learning tutoring, served as academic advisor and poster presentation referee.
  • Professional Service – Member of the Egyptian Medical Syndicate, ARVO and American Heart Association; former executive member of the Institutional Review Board of Mansoura Faculty of Medicine (2020). Invited reviewer for journals including Experimental Eye Research, Scientific Reports, Inflammation and Investigative Ophthalmology & Visual Science.

Prof. Naglaa was promoted to Professor at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls in 2015 and at Cairo University in 2018. With over 30 years of teaching experience, she has held various leadership positions in both institutions, including Head of the Admission Committee, Student Affairs, Curriculum Development, Faculty Development, and Research Unit. She also served as Chief Academic Officer at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls and finally as Associate Dean of Academic Affairs, at Dubai Pharmacy College for Girls.

Prof. Naglaa is a member of the American Society of Pharmacognosy and holds certifications in nutrition and health. She introduced a pioneering course on “Natural Medicines, Safety, and Efficacy” at Dubai Pharmacy College, which focuses on drug-herb interactions and supplement quality control, a first of its kind in the Arab region. Her role as Associate Dean of Academic Affairs has provided her with extensive experience in community, industrial, and hospital training, enabling her to collaborate effectively with training heads at Dubai Pharmacy College.

Prof. Naglaa has received prestigious research awards from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Amsterdam in the field of Natural Products. She has been recognized among the top two thousand scientists in the UAE. As a reviewer for numerous international journals in natural products, she has published over 40 scientific papers in impact factor journals. To continuously advance her career, she regularly participates in workshops, seminars, webinars, and conferences in the field of education.

She holds a Bachelor of Pharmacy with Honors, two master’s degrees in Pharmaceutical Technology and Health Administration, and a PhD in Pharmaceutical Technology.

Her research focuses on advanced drug delivery systems, including proniosomes, nanocarriers, microsponges, buccal films, in situ gels, and strategies to improve drug solubility, stability, and bioavailability.

Dr. Sammour has published several peer-reviewed research articles and supervised student research projects in pharmaceutical formulation, and drug delivery. She is also actively involved in academic leadership, curriculum development, student affairs, academic advising, and institutional committees.

Her current interests include integrating artificial intelligence and emerging technologies into pharmaceutical sciences, drug delivery research, and higher education to support innovation and future-ready pharmacy graduates.

Biography

Dr. Rania Hamed Shalaby is an Egyptian pharmacologist, medical educator, and academic leader with over 18 years of distinguished service. She obtained her M.B.B.Ch. (2005), M.Sc. Biography

Prof. Kassab is Professor of Physiology and Medical Education and serves as Associate Dean for Academics at the College of Medicine, Dubai Medical University. He also holds a professorship at the Faculty of Medicine, Suez Canal University, Egypt. Over his distinguished career, he has held several senior academic leadership roles, including Acting Dean of the College of Medicine at Gulf Medical University (2025), Associate Dean for Academic Affairs at Qatar University (2017–2020), Vice Dean for Academic Affairs at the Arabian Gulf University (2005–2009, 2010–2013), and Chairman of the Department of Medical Education at Suez Canal University (2013–2016). He also served as Professor of Physiology at RCSI–Medical University of Bahrain.

A Fellow of the Academy of Medical Educators, Prof. Kassab serves on the Executive Committee of the Association of Medical Education in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (AMEEMR), affiliated with the World Federation for Medical Education (WFME), and has worked as a WHO consultant in medical education and accreditation. He sits on the editorial boards of leading journals, including BMC Medical Education and Health Professions Education. Widely recognized for his scholarly contributions, he has delivered numerous workshops and published over 85 peer-reviewed papers in physiology and medical education.

name: Dr. Shifan Khanday
title: Associate ProfessorAssociate Dean of Research & Head of AI & Smart Education
bio:
Biography

Dr. Shifan Khanday is a physician, anatomist, and academic leader specializing in the integration of artificial intelligence within medical education.She holds dual doctorates—a Ph.D. from St George’s and Kingston University of London (UK) and a Doctorate in Anatomy from Sri Ramachandra Medical University —A Diplomate in Family Medicine with Royal College of Physicians ,London ,United Kingdom she also holds Master’s degrees in Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare ( Spain) and a Master’s in Health Professions Education (Maastricht University, Netherlands). A qualified Family Medicine physician with an MBA in Healthcare leadership she combines clinical insight with advanced expertise in digital transformation and higher-education innovation.

At Dubai Medical University, Dr. Khanday leads the university’s strategic transformation in AI-driven medical education, overseeing the development and governance of AI-based education and research systems. Under her direction, DMU became the first medical university in the UAE to integrate GPT-powered agents within its Learning Management System and to integrate AI in curriculum reform .She has conceptualized and implemented several institutional initiatives, including the AI Xcelerate Hackathon, AI Integration in Curriculum and Research Writing Pilot, and E-Tuesdays Innovation Series, promoting AI literacy and innovation across the academic community. Her scholarly and leadership excellence earned her a nomination for the UNESCO King Hamad Bin Isa Al-Khalifa Prize for the Use of ICT in Education, recognizing her contributions to technology-enabled learning and equitable access to education. Dr. Khanday is the author of Quick Revision in Anatomy (CBS Publishers, 2014) and AI and I: Basics of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Medical Education (2023). She has presented her research Nationally and continues to pioneer research at the intersection of healthcare, education, and emerging technologies.

Teaching & Service

bio:
Biography

Dr. Nadia Mahmoud Mohamed Ali El Rouby is a distinguished Egyptian medical educator and histologist with an extensive academic and research background spanning more than three decades. She obtained her M.B.B.Ch. from Cairo University in 1985, followed by an M.Sc. (1990) and Ph.D. (1994) in Histology, and a Postgraduate Diploma in Pediatrics (1995). In 2017, she completed master’s in medical education (JMHPE) from Maastricht University, Netherlands, in collaboration with Suez Canal University, Egypt, ranking second in her class. Currently, she is working as Professor and Head of biomedical sciences Department at Dubai Medical University, College of Medicine. She also holds leadership roles such as Associate Dean of Student Affairs and Admissions and Head of Curriculum Review and Program Delivery Committees.

Her research contributions cover a wide range of histological and pathological studies, focusing on endocrine, hepatic, and reproductive systems, as well as innovative educational methodologies. Dr. El Rouby’s recent publications in international peer-reviewed journals underscore her ongoing commitment to biomedical science and education, particularly her interest in exploring natural remedies and drug safety at the cellular level.

bio:
Biography

Dr. Samia M. H. Farghaly is Professor and Head of the Primary Health Care Division at the College of Medicine and Specialist Senior Registrar at the Dubai Health Authority from 2004-2016 . With over five decades of distinguished service—spanning Bahrain (1978–2004) and the United Arab Emirates (2004–present)—she is recognized as a pioneer of Family Medicine education in the Gulf region and a leading advocate of the biopsychosocial model of care.
Her journey began in 1983 when she became the first Family Physician to qualify from Bahrain’s postgraduate Family Medicine Program, developed with the American University of Beirut. This landmark achievement preceded the establishment of the Arab Board of Family Medicine (1987) and was recognized as equivalent to consultant-level training. In 1992, she completed a Master’s in Psychiatry at Dublin University, strengthening her integration of psychological care within clinical practice.
During her 25-year tenure in Bahrain, Dr. Farghaly served as Consultant Family Physician and Maternal & Child Health Supervisor, leading antenatal, immunization, and family-planning services. She was also Faculty Tutor in the Postgraduate Family Medicine Residency Program and Undergraduate Instructor at the Arabian Gulf University, teaching clinical skills, communication, and patient-centered care. As an Examiner for the Arab Board, she contributed to OSCE design and assessment, training generations of family physicians across the region.
In Dubai, she practices family medicine in DHA 2 days/week and teaching family medicine residency program in Dubai for 3rd and 4th year resident preparing them for Arab board and participate in Arab board exam she helped establish the MRCGP [International] Examination, became Accredited Examiner (2005), and led the MCQ Module (2006–2012). At Dubai Medical College, she founded the Primary Health Care Division (2007), developed its curriculum, and created the Simulation Center.
Internationally, she remains an Accredited Examiner and Standard-Setting Panel Member for the MRCGP, advancing academic and clinical excellence globally.

bio:
Biography

Prof. Dr. Fahad Saqib Lodhi, PhD, MPH, MBBS, is a distinguished epidemiologist and public health leader with over 20 years of experience in clinical and community health. Currently serving as Professor and Chair of the Department of Public Health and Behavioral Sciences at Dubai Medical University, UAE (since August 2023), he drives innovative curricula, research, and community outreach focused on non-communicable diseases (NCDs), mental health, and health equity in conflict-affected regions. Previously, he held professorial roles at Women Medical and Dental College, Abbottabad, Pakistan (2020–2023), and contributed as a Public Health Specialist in Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Health (2016–2020), where he supervised postgraduate training and community interventions.

Dr. Lodhi’s PhD from Tehran University of Medical Sciences (2018) emphasized epidemiology and biostatistics, building on his MPH (2009) and MBBS (2004) from Pakistan. A prolific researcher, he has authored over 25 peer-reviewed publications, exploring quality of life, COVID-19 impacts, and psychosocial factors in vulnerable populations. His work integrates behavioral theories with data-driven advocacy, particularly for marginalized groups like refugees and low-SES communities. Committed to mentorship, he has supervised numerous theses and edited journals like the Journal of Women Medical & Dental College. Dr. Lodhi’s expertise bridges academia, policy, and practice, advancing NCD prevention in the MENA region.

bio:
Biography

Ms. Hala joined Dubai Medical College in 2025 as a full-time lecturer in the nursing program. She earned her Bachelor of Nursing Science from Mut’ah University, Jordan, a Master in Pediatric Nursing from Mut’ah University, Jordan.

Ms. Hala has over 15 years of diverse nursing and academic experience across clinical, humanitarian, and educational settings in the Middle East. She began her career as a registered nurse in Jordan, working in emergency and pediatric wards at Karak Governmental Hospital and the Arab Medical Center, where she gained frontline experience in acute and general pediatric care. She then specialized in pediatric nursing at King Abdulaziz Medical City, Saudi Arabia, with a focus on renal and endocrine care, and later transitioned into health informatics as an Application Analyst for the nursing module of the Clinical Information Management System.

Her humanitarian experience includes serving with the International Medical Corps at the Azraq Refugee Camp, where she provided pediatric care in crisis conditions. In academia, Hala has taught and supervised nursing students since 2017, first at Mut’ah University in Jordan, and since 2021 as a Clinical Instructor at the Higher Colleges of Technology in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE. In these roles, she has led clinical training, mentored students, and integrated digital learning platforms into blended instruction.
